prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat electronic bands in twisted bilayer graphene at a magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in moire flat-band systems

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is the clearest case on the shortlist of a discovery found by listening to nature after a sharp theoretical prediction. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model (2011) located the magic angle, and the 2018 observations of correlated insulators and superconductivity in Jarillo-Herrero's group showed that the prediction opened a real, tunable regime of quantum matter instead of a mathematical curiosity. Seven of eight members place it in their top three, and the colleagues who rank it differ in field (electronic structure, statistical physics, materials, atomic physics), which suggests the case does not depend on one subfield's taste. The core phenomenology has been reproduced by many independent groups and extended to other moire systems, so this is a field-defining result and not a single-lab claim. The theory-plus-experiment split also maps naturally onto the three supplied names.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is timing and interpretation: the field is only about eight years old, the origin of the superconductivity and of several correlated states is still debated, and sample-to-sample variability remains. There is also a genuine attribution gap, since the 2018 experimental breakthrough was a group effort and Cory Dean's hBN-encapsulated devices and other later experiments are not in the supplied credit. If the committee judges that the experimental credit cannot be fairly limited to Jarillo-Herrero, the three-name configuration is weaker than it looks. I accept this, but I do not think it justifies delaying a discovery whose central phenomena are already robust.

responses.point: B022 is well verified but young, with the superconducting mechanism and sample variability unresolved, so recognition could be slightly premature. He ranks it only sixth and prefers B038 and B012.
responses.response: I take the maturity worry seriously, but it concerns the interpretation of the superconductivity and not the discovery. The Nobel criterion is a discovery whose existence is secure and whose consequences are large, and correlated insulators and superconductivity near the magic angle have been measured in many laboratories and device geometries. We have honoured earlier results before their microscopic explanation was settled. I also disagree that B038 is clearly stronger on discovery grounds. Quantum key distribution is a conceptual protocol whose lasting merit is real, but it was largely a proposal, while the moire work combines a prediction with a measured phenomenon. I do share his Dean credit concern and keep it as an open attribution point.

responses.point: He ranks optical lattice clocks (B012) first: a clean two-person Katori-Ye attribution, independent confirmation at 10^-18 across laboratories, and no timing risk because the redefinition of the second does not affect the discovery.
responses.response: I agree that B012 has the cleanest attribution on the list and is genuinely mature, and that is why I keep it as my first alternative. Where I differ is on what the discovery adds. A precision instrument achieves an extraordinary improvement of an existing capability, while B022 opened a new class of phenomena that nobody could predict in detail, which fits a prize for finding something in nature better. I do not think clean attribution should outweigh scope. If the committee decides that the credit problem for B022 is unresolvable, B012 is where I would move, and I would not need to be persuaded further.

responses.point: He ranks B022 first as a theory-to-experiment story whose phenomenology is stable after eight years of reproduction, and notes that the supplied names may not match every committee view of who was decisive.
responses.response: I agree with the scientific reading and with the caution on credit. Where I want to add something is that his qualification about the experimental names is more than a footnote. If we write the citation around the prediction of the magic angle and the discovery of correlated and superconducting states, as I have, we remain consistent with the supplied names without claiming that nobody else mattered. I would resist widening the citation to cover all moire platforms, because that invites the very attribution dispute we want to avoid.

responses.point: He ranks B022 first and B018 second, seeing the magic-angle result as a case where calculated band structure anticipated a new phase, and sees topological insulators as well confirmed, mature and arguably overdue, but he flags the missing Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang credit.
responses.response: I agree on B022 and I share his view that the BHZ omission is the real obstacle for B018. I would go slightly further: the 2016 prize already honoured topological phases of matter, and with Zhang deceased, the theory side of HgTe cannot be restored within the supplied strings. The experimental confirmation in HgTe is clear, but I do not think the committee can in good conscience name Kane, Mele and Molenkamp while leaving out the prediction that guided Molenkamp's experiment. That is why B018 sits below B022 for me, though it remains a serious option.

responses.point: She ranks B012 first and Cirac-Zoller (B061) second, describing B061 as a clean two-person theory prize that is arguably overdue, with the overlap with B056 and B004 to be resolved in the citation wording.
responses.response: B061 has a clean attribution and real conceptual weight, but it was not ranked highly enough to make the shortlist, so I do not think we can build a configuration on it here. More importantly, it is a blueprint, with the experimental realisations largely recognised in 2012, while B022 has both halves of the story to hand. I do agree that if the committee turns toward trapped-ion and atom-array theory, the overlap with B056 would have to be handled very carefully.

uncertainties: Whether the experimental credit can be fairly limited to Jarillo-Herrero within a three-person cap, given Dean's hBN-based devices and other groups' independent early reproductions.
Whether the committee regards the unsettled mechanism of the superconductivity as a maturity problem or only as an open follow-up question.

How much weight the 2016 topological-phases prize should carry when comparing B022 and B018, and how the choice between a new-phenomenon prize (B022) and a precision-instrument prize (B012) should be made.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my provided profile. My research is in string theory, quantum gravity and cosmology, and my documented connections (David Gross, Hector Rubinstein, Thomas Van Riet, the Uppsala theoretical-physics group) do not link me to any of the shortlisted candidates. I am a black-hole theorist and for that reason rank B027 as an alternative; I flag that as a disciplinary preference, not a personal connection.
